tour.title: Galata Tower — once the Tower of Christ
tour.text: The Genoese, settled in Galata since 1267, rebuilt the tower in 1348–49 and called it Christea Turris, the Tower of Christ.

tour.title: Bodrum Mosque — the Myrelaion
tour.text: Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos built the Myrelaion as his family's burial church (first burial 922). Around 1500 Grand Vizier Mesih Pasha made it a mosque.

tour.title: Arap Mosque — San Paolo e Domenico
tour.text: A Dominican church of the Latin community in Galata, enlarged in 1307. The Dominicans left in 1475; the name 'Arap' most likely comes from the Moors resettled here after 1492.

tour.title: Beyoğlu — Pera, 'the other side'
tour.text: OSM still keeps Pera, the old name of the district across the Golden Horn from the historic peninsula.

tour.title: SALT Galata — the Imperial Ottoman Bank
tour.text: Designed by Alexandre Vallaury as the headquarters of the Imperial Ottoman Bank, which used it from 1892 to 1999. Reopened as SALT Galata in November 2011.

tour.title: Four Seasons Sultanahmet — the Sultanahmet Jail
tour.text: Built as a prison in 1918–19, abandoned in 1969, opened as a hotel in 1996.

tour.title: 15 July Martyrs' Bridge — the Bosphorus Bridge
tour.text: On 25 July 2016 the cabinet renamed the Bosphorus Bridge to commemorate the civilians killed opposing the 15 July coup attempt.

tour.title: Yeşilköy — Ayastefanos, San Stefano
tour.text: In 1924 the poet Halid Ziya Uşaklıgil proposed 'Yeşilköy', green village, for the suburb known as Ayastefanos / San Stefano.

tour.title: Polonezköy — Adampol
tour.text: Founded in 1842 on the initiative of Prince Adam Czartoryski for Polish émigrés, and named Adampol after him.
